action: If you receive a Geisinger notice, accept the free identity theft protection offered and be alert to emails or calls that use your medical record details.
exec: A small, contained email-account compromise at a large health system; limited data types and no financial identifiers.
plain: A Pennsylvania hospital system says a break-in to one staff email account may have exposed basic details of fewer than 2,000 patients.
summary: The Pennsylvania health system issued a breach notice dated November 16 saying suspicious activity found on August 20 in one employee's email account may have led to theft of some patient information. Fewer than 2,000 people are affected. Data covers names, birth dates, medical record numbers, service dates and insurer names; no Social Security or financial data was involved.
title: Geisinger notifies patients after suspicious activity in an employee email account

validation.note: One trade outlet reporting the health system's notice.

review.note: Compared 16 Nov notice, 20 Aug detection, one employee account, under 2,000, data types against HIPAA Journal
